items.author: Sydney Allen
items.title: The ongoing efforts to get ecocide recognized at the International Criminal Court
items.summary: For the nations that started this, the stakes are not abstract. They are asking the world to build infrastructure to prosecute and prevent harm that is already happening to them.

items.author: Jo Carter
items.title: Why Japan’s anti-hate measures fall short
items.summary: The prevalence of online hate speech is to a large extent related to a lack of effective domestic legislation and human rights education.

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: Family stories keep alive Georgia’s democratic past and the memory of Soviet repression
items.summary: “Family stories can open up broader conversations about democracy, human rights, repression, and civic responsibility”

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: In Moldova, teens are learning about democracy and elections through an app
items.summary: VotEDU started off as a civic-education project to help young people understand democracy before they vote for the first time.

items.author: Global Voices Announcements
items.title: Support Global Voices’ December Spotlight: Digital Communities
items.summary: In this month’s spotlight, Global Voices, in partnership with Ranking Digital Rights, will explore the multiverse of digital communities — starting with our own.

items.author: The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL)
items.title: An AI chatbot can explain your rights. But can it get you justice?
items.summary: AI could make the law easier to navigate. But the real test is whether it helps people resolve the problems they face, not simply access information about their rights.

items.author: Hong Kong Free Press
items.title: ‘Who will respond?’: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong fears being forgotten amid 10-year sentence
items.summary: The 30-year-old pro-democracy activist has spent almost six years behind bars and was set for release in January 2026, until authorities charged him with conspiring to foreign collusion last year.

items.author: Forus
items.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
items.summary: A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams — and why the crisis goes far beyond money.

items.author: Jude Pierre Louis
items.title: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
items.summary: Street medicine vendors have no professional medical training — and the drugs they sell in questionable conditions on the street pose a serious danger to consumers’ lives.

items.title: In win against impunity, Indonesian court orders the reform of Military Justice Law
items.summary: "Justice for civilian victims of military abuses shouldn’t be blocked by an unfair military court system."
